title: Wide-swing cascode mirror
description: The low-voltage cascode mirror. It keeps the matched-$V_{DS}$ accuracy of a cascode mirror but recovers the output swing a standard cascode wastes. The trick is the cascode gate bias: instead of the two-diode stack (which parks the mirror node a full $V_{GS}$ above ground), a single diode-connected NMOS at a low inversion level, carrying its own programmed current, sets a bias $V_{bias}$ that places the reference node about one saturation voltage and a small margin above ground. The output then only has to clear two stacked saturation voltages and that margin, with no threshold overhead, so the output can swing far lower than a standard cascode's $V_{GS} + V_{dsat}$ floor. Four devices are drawn. In the reference branch the reference mirror device carries the input current with its drain on the reference node, and the reference cascode stands on that node with its gate on $V_{bias}$ and its drain on the gate the two mirror devices share, where the input current enters. The bias diode is drawn, and $V_{bias}$ is its gate-source voltage. The reference node is solved under it: it sits where the reference cascode's gate-source voltage hangs it under $V_{bias}$, so wherever the design is held it moves with the devices, as silicon's does. The bias diode's inversion level is the knob that places it, and an advisory check reports how far above the reference device's saturation voltage the node lands, against the node_margin the generator is designed to leave. The output branch is drawn as the cascode current mirror draws it: the output mirror device is K times the reference device's width on the reference device's gate, with its current read off the table at its own drain voltage; the output cascode is K times the reference cascode's width on $V_{bias}$, in series with it and carrying that current; and the node between them is solved so that the gate-source voltage the cascode needs for that current hangs the node under $V_{bias}$. That node equals the reference node only where the output sits level with the reference cascode's drain; elsewhere it settles a few millivolts away, and the systematic-error row reports what that costs. The sheet's own device is the output cascode; the other three are blocks. Random matching is the Pelgrom spread of the bottom mirror pair; the cascodes only pass the current and so do not set the ratio.

params.name: I_in
params.note: reference current

params.name: K
params.note: mirror ratio W_out/W_ref (a unit-device multiple)

params.name: VDD
params.note: supply

params.name: V_out
params.note: DC level of the node the mirror serves, which is the output cascode's drain; the wide-swing floor lets this go low, and the output cascode's saturation region holds it above the node under the cascode plus the cascode's saturation voltage

params.name: L
params.note: mirror-device length

params.name: L_c
params.note: cascode-device length

params.name: gm_id_m
params.note: mirror inversion: lower gm/ID (higher V*) tightens matching but raises the saturation voltage the node sits at; the default keeps the compliance floor under the V_out default even on a high-V* device

params.name: gm_id_c
params.note: cascode inversion, set on the reference cascode. The output cascode takes K times that device's width and the output mirror device's current, so its own inversion level is read off the table

params.name: vds_lo
params.note: the reference node: the reference mirror device's drain and the reference cascode's source. Solved, not set: the reference cascode's gate is the bias diode's, so this is the node that hangs the cascode's own gate-source voltage under it; gm_id_cb is the knob that moves it. The stored value is never read. It is searched between ground and 0.6 V: the node sits below the gate the mirror devices share, one reference gate-source voltage above ground, which the wiring cannot place before the design is sized, and above 0.6 V the reference cascode would have no drain-source voltage left on either table

params.name: gm_id_cb
params.note: inversion level of the cascode bias diode. Its gate-source voltage is V_bias, so a lower gm/ID raises the cascode gates and the reference node under them: the default parks the node about node_margin above the reference device's knee

params.name: I_cb
params.note: the current the cascode bias diode is programmed to. A diode at a given inversion level sits at one gate-source voltage whatever its current, so this sets only its width

params.name: k_x
params.note: where the node between the two output devices — the output mirror device's drain and the output cascode's source — sits, as a fraction of the cascode gate bias V_bias. Solved, not set: the current the output mirror device delivers at that node is the current the output cascode carries, and the gate-source voltage the cascode needs for that current hangs the node under V_bias. The engine searches for the node at which the two agree; the stored value is never read. It is stated as a fraction of V_bias so that its range means the same thing whatever the table: the node lies above ground, 0, and below the cascode gate by at least the cascode's threshold, so the range stops at 0.8 rather than at the gate itself, 1 — which also keeps the middle of the range, where the search first looks, inside the stretch where the output cascode has a drain-source voltage when the drawn bias sits high, at a slow, hot condition. Where the output sits level with the reference cascode's drain the node is the reference node vds_lo; it settles a little below or above that where the output sits lower or higher. The V_x row gives the node in volts

params.name: node_margin
params.note: how far above the mirror devices' saturation knee the wide-swing bias is designed to park the node — the customary 50-100 mV that keeps the mirror out of triode across corners. The node-margin check compares the node the drawn bias produces against it

params.name: avt
params.note: Pelgrom A_VT from the PDK

params.name: abeta
params.note: Pelgrom A_beta from the PDK

params.name: err_target
params.note: systematic (lambda) error budget

params.name: match_target
params.note: 1-sigma random ratio-error budget

doc.title: Reference mirror device (bottom)
doc.description: The bottom reference device at the input current — the one device on this sheet whose current is typed. Its drain is the reference node and its gate is the reference cascode's drain, where the input current enters. Its saturation voltage sets where the reference node should sit, so it has to stay saturated there. It publishes its width and its gate voltage, which is all the output mirror device needs to copy it.

params.name: vds_r
params.note: the reference node

doc.title: Reference cascode
doc.description: The cascode in the reference branch, carrying the reference current, read from the reference device rather than typed. Its gate is the cascode bias, its source the reference node, and its drain the gate the two mirror devices share, so its drain-source voltage is the reference device's gate-source voltage less the reference node. Its source stands on the reference node rather than the bulk, so its body bias is declared as that node. Its gate-source voltage above the reference node is the cascode bias the wide-swing generator has to produce; the output cascode takes K times its width.

params.name: vds_cc
params.note: from the reference node up to the gate the two mirror devices share

params.name: vsb_cc
params.note: the source stands on the reference node, not the bulk

doc.title: Output mirror device (bottom)
doc.description: The output-branch mirror device: K times the reference device's width on the reference device's gate, with its source at ground like the reference's. Its current is read off the table rather than typed — the reference sits at the reference node and this device at the node under the output cascode, so it delivers K times the reference current scaled by what that difference in $V_{DS}$ does through its $g_{ds}$. That current is the output current: the cascode above is in series and carries it. Its own output resistance is what degenerates the cascode.

params.name: W_o
params.note: K times the reference device's width

params.name: vgs_o
params.note: the reference device's gate voltage — the gate wire the two share

params.name: vds_o
params.note: the node under the output cascode

equations.name: node_headroom
equations.note: how far above the reference device's saturation knee the drawn bias parks the reference node

equations.name: V_bias
equations.note: the cascode gate bias both cascodes share: the bias diode's gate-source voltage, the level of the wire its gate and drain sit on. The reference node hangs one reference-cascode gate-source voltage under it

equations.name: V_x
equations.note: the node between the two output devices, in volts: the solved fraction of the cascode gate bias. It is the output mirror device's drain voltage and the output cascode's body bias, and what is left of the output level above it is the cascode's drain-source voltage. With the fraction solved it is the cascode gate bias less the output cascode's gate-source voltage

equations.name: k_casc
equations.note: where the output cascode's gate puts its source, as a fraction of the cascode gate bias: that bias, less the gate-source voltage the cascode needs to carry the output mirror device's current at the body bias and drain voltage the node gives it. k_x is solved to this

equations.name: I_out
equations.note: the current delivered at the output: the output cascode's, which is the current the output mirror device below it delivers — the two are in series

equations.name: sys_err
equations.note: lambda mismatch between the two mirror devices: the reference device sits at the reference node and the output mirror device at the solved node under the output cascode. The two agree where the output is level with the reference cascode's drain. Elsewhere the cascode takes up nearly all of the difference between the two levels, the node moves by the millivolts that are left, and the error is those millivolts through the mirror device's gds

equations.name: V_out_min
equations.note: the output compliance floor: the node under the output cascode plus the cascode's own saturation voltage — two stacked saturation voltages and the node margin, with no threshold overhead (contrast vgs + vdsat for a standard cascode). The output cascode's saturation region holds the output above it

equations.name: irel_out
equations.note: current spread of the output mirror device, at the inversion level it lands on through the gate it shares with the reference

equations.name: sigma_ratio
equations.note: random 1-sigma error of the K:1 ratio from the bottom mirror pair; the K-times-larger output device contributes 1/sqrt(K) of the reference spread

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: output resistance of the output branch, with the output cascode read at the current it carries and with its source on the solved node. The mirror device's own r_o sits in the cascode's source, so local series feedback multiplies the cascode's r_o by (1 + (g_m + g_mb)*r_o) and that degenerating resistance adds back in series; both source-referred generators feed back through it, so gmb belongs inside the factor — the same form the source-degenerated mirror uses with a resistor in that role. This is the number a stage loading the mirror sees

checks.note: the cascode inversion level against the ceiling of the data the output cascode is read from. The output cascode is given a width and a current, so its own level is an outcome; the reference device and the reference cascode, which are sized for an inversion level, carry the same check on their own data

the margin the bias is designed to leave above the reference device's knee. Advisory: the reference device's own saturation check is the hard one, and a node a few millivolts short of the design margin is a retune of the bias diode, not a broken mirror
